title: Impact of Close-Election Incumbency on Reelection Probability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**

This is a classic RDD setup. The running variable is the vote-share margin, and the treatment (incumbency) is determined by whether this margin crosses a cutoff. Candidates who barely win (margin just above the cutoff) are compared to those who barely lose (margin just below the cutoff).

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Continuity assumption:** In the absence of treatment, potential outcomes are continuous at the cutoff. Candidates just above and just below the threshold are comparable in all respects except treatment status.
2. **No manipulation:** Candidates cannot precisely manipulate their vote-share margin to sort around the cutoff (testable via McCrary density test).
3. **Local randomization:** Near the cutoff, winning vs. losing is essentially random, creating a quasi-experimental setting.

The cutoff appears to be around 0.5 (the median vote share where winning transitions to losing), based on the data showing `treated=1` for values above ~0.5 and `treated=0` for values below. I'll verify this empirically.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# RDD Analysis: Incumbency Advantage in Close Elections
# ============================================================

# Load required libraries
if (!require("rdrobust")) install.packages("rdrobust", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("rddensity")) install.packages("rddensity", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# --------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s88_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "x", ncol(df), "\n")
summary(df)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Determine the cutoff
# --------------------------------------------------
# Check the relationship between running_var and treated
cat("\n=== Identifying the Cutoff ===\n")
cat("Min running_var for treated=1:", min(df$running_var[df$treated == 1]), "\n")
cat("Max running_var for treated=0:", max(df$running_var[df$treated == 0]), "\n")

# The cutoff appears to be at 0.5
cutoff <- 0.5

# Verify: check if treated is deterministic function of running_var >= cutoff
df$predicted_treat <- as.integer(df$running_var >= cutoff)
cat("Perfect compliance with cutoff=0.5:", all(df$predicted_treat == df$treated), "\n")

# If not 0.5, try to find the actual cutoff
if (!all(df$predicted_treat == df$treated)) {
  # Find the cutoff by looking at the boundary
  max_untreated <- max(df$running_var[df$treated == 0])
  min_treated <- min(df$running_var[df$treated == 1])
  cutoff <- (max_untreated + min_treated) / 2
  cat("Estimated cutoff:", cutoff, "\n")
  df$predicted_treat <- as.integer(df$running_var >= cutoff)
  cat("Perfect compliance with estimated cutoff:", all(df$predicted_treat == df$treated), "\n")
}

# Center running variable at the cutoff
df$X <- df$running_var - cutoff

cat("\n=== Distribution around cutoff ===\n")
cat("Observations below cutoff (lost):", sum(df$X < 0), "\n")
cat("Observations above cutoff (won):", sum(df$X >= 0), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Visualization
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Visual Inspection ===\n")

# Binned scatter plot
pdf("rdd_plot.pdf", width = 10, height = 6)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Raw scatter
plot(df$X, df$y, pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     col = ifelse(df$treated == 1, "steelblue", "coral"),
     xlab = "Vote Margin (centered)", ylab = "Reelection Probability (y)",
     main = "RDD: Incumbency Effect on Reelection")
abline(v = 0, lty = 2, lwd = 2)

# Binned means
n_bins <- 20
df$bin <- cut(df$X, breaks = n_bins)
bin_means <- aggregate(y ~ bin, data = df, FUN = mean)
bin_x <- aggregate(X ~ bin, data = df, FUN = mean)
bin_data <- merge(bin_x, bin_means, by = "bin")
plot(bin_data$X, bin_data$y, pch = 19, cex = 1.5,
     col = ifelse(bin_data$X >= 0, "steelblue", "coral"),
     xlab = "Vote Margin (centered)", ylab = "Mean Reelection Probability",
     main = "Binned Scatter Plot")
abline(v = 0, lty = 2, lwd = 2)

# Add local polynomial fits on each side
left <- df[df$X < 0, ]
right <- df[df$X >= 0, ]
if (nrow(left) > 3) {
  fit_left <- lm(y ~ poly(X, 2), data = left)
  x_left <- seq(min(left$X), 0, length.out = 100)
  pred_left <- predict(fit_left, newdata = data.frame(X = x_left))
  lines(x_left, pred_left, col = "coral", lwd = 2)
}
if (nrow(right) > 3) {
  fit_right <- lm(y ~ poly(X, 2), data = right)
  x_right <- seq(0, max(right$X), length.out = 100)
  pred_right <- predict(fit_right, newdata = data.frame(X = x_right))
  lines(x_right, pred_right, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
dev.off()
cat("Plot saved to rdd_plot.pdf\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Main RDD Analysis using rdrobust
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS (rdrobust) ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# MSE-optimal bandwidth, local linear
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
summary(rd_main)

cat("\n--- Key Results ---\n")
cat("RDD Estimate (Local Linear):", round(rd_main$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust 95% CI: [", round(rd_main$ci[3, 1], 4), ",", round(rd_main$ci[3, 2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_main$pv[3], 4), "\n")
cat("Bandwidth (h):", round(rd_main$bws[1, 1], 4), "\n")
cat("Eff. N (left):", rd_main$N_h[1], " Eff. N (right):", rd_main$N_h[2], "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness Checks
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# 5a. Local quadratic polynomial
cat("\n--- Robustness 1: Local Quadratic (p=2) ---\n")
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "triangular", p = 2)
cat("RDD Estimate (Quadratic):", round(rd_quad$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_quad$pv[3], 4), "\n")

# 5b. Different kernels
cat("\n--- Robustness 2: Uniform Kernel ---\n")
rd_uniform <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "uniform", p = 1)
cat("RDD Estimate (Uniform):", round(rd_uniform$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_uniform$pv[3], 4), "\n")

cat("\n--- Robustness 3: Epanechnikov Kernel ---\n")
rd_epan <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "epanechnikov", p = 1)
cat("RDD Estimate (Epanechnikov):", round(rd_epan$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_epan$pv[3], 4), "\n")

# 5c. Half and double bandwidth
cat("\n--- Robustness 4: Half Bandwidth ---\n")
h_main <- rd_main$bws[1, 1]
rd_half <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "triangular", p = 1, h = h_main / 2)
cat("RDD Estimate (h/2):", round(rd_half$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_half$pv[3], 4), "\n")

cat("\n--- Robustness 5: Double Bandwidth ---\n")
rd_double <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = "triangular", p = 1, h = h_main * 2)
cat("RDD Estimate (2h):", round(rd_double$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_double$pv[3], 4), "\n")

# 5d. Parametric approach near the cutoff
cat("\n--- Robustness 6: Parametric OLS (narrow window) ---\n")
narrow <- df[abs(df$X) <= h_main, ]
ols_narrow <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = narrow)
cat("OLS Estimate:", round(coef(ols_narrow)["treated"], 4), "\n")
cat("Std. Error:", round(summary(ols_narrow)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(summary(ols_narrow)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")

# 5e. Using near_cutoff subsample
cat("\n--- Robustness 7: Using near_cutoff subsample ---\n")
near <- df[df$near_cutoff == 1, ]
cat("N observations near cutoff:", nrow(near), "\n")
if (nrow(near) > 20) {
  rd_near <- rdrobust(y = near$y, x = near$X, c = 0, kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
  cat("RDD Estimate (near cutoff):", round(rd_near$coef[1], 4), "\n")
  cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_near$pv[3], 4), "\n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Manipulation Test (McCrary)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== MANIPULATION TEST ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
density_test <- rddensity(df$X, c = 0)
cat("McCrary-type density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")
if (density_test$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("=> No evidence of manipulation at the cutoff (p > 0.05)\n")
} else {
  cat("=> Warning: Evidence of possible manipulation (p < 0.05)\n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Placebo / Falsification Tests
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== PLACEBO TESTS (Fake Cutoffs) ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Test at fake cutoffs
fake_cutoffs <- c(-0.25, -0.15, 0.15, 0.25)
for (fc in fake_cutoffs) {
  rd_placebo <- tryCatch({
    rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = fc, kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(rd_placebo)) {
    cat("Placebo cutoff at", fc, ": Estimate =", round(rd_placebo$coef[1], 4),
        ", p-value =", round(rd_placebo$pv[3], 4), "\n")
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 8. Summary Table
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF ALL ESTIMATES ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

results <- data.frame(
  Specification = c("Main (Local Linear, Triangular)",
                     "Local Quadratic",
                     "Uniform Kernel",
                     "Epanechnikov Kernel",
                     "Half Bandwidth",
                     "Double Bandwidth",
                     "Parametric OLS (narrow)"),
  Estimate = round(c(rd_main$coef[1], rd_quad$coef[1], rd_uniform$coef[1],
                      rd_epan$coef[1], rd_half$coef[1], rd_double$coef[1],
                      coef(ols_narrow)["treated"]), 4),
  Robust_pvalue = round(c(rd_main$pv[3], rd_quad$pv[3], rd_uniform$pv[3],
                           rd_epan$pv[3], rd_half$pv[3], rd_double$pv[3],
                           summary(ols_narrow)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"]), 4)
)
print(results)

cat("\n=== CONCLUSION ===\n")
main_est <- rd_main$coef[1]
main_pv <- rd_main$pv[3]
if (main_pv < 0.05) {
  cat("The RDD estimate of", round(main_est, 4),
      "is statistically significant (robust p =", round(main_pv, 4), ").\n")
  if (main_est > 0) {
    cat("Barely winning an election INCREASES reelection probability.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Barely winning an election DECREASES reelection probability.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("The RDD estimate of", round(main_est, 4),
      "is NOT statistically significant (robust p =", round(main_pv, 4), ").\n")
  cat("No evidence of an incumbency advantage/disadvantage from barely winning.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign and magnitude:** I expect a **positive** RDD estimate, likely in the range of **0.10–0.40** (representing a 10–40 percentage point increase in reelection probability from barely winning).

**Reasoning:**
1. **Incumbency advantage literature:** The classic Lee (2008) RDD study of U.S. House elections finds a substantial incumbency advantage of roughly 40–45 percentage points. Barely winning grants access to office resources, media visibility, fundraising advantages, and name recognition that boost future electoral performance.

2. **Data patterns:** Looking at the preview, treated observations (running_var > cutoff) tend to have positive y values while untreated observations have negative y values, suggesting a positive discontinuity at the cutoff.

3. **Robustness:** I expect the estimate to be fairly stable across specifications (different bandwidths, kernels, polynomial orders), and the McCrary density

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze the discontinuity at the vote-share cutoff to isolate the effect of incumbency.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Winning a close election reduces the probability of reelection.
